papers.title: Asymmetric cross-reactivity of nuclear receptors reveals an evolutionary buffer between estrogen and androgen signaling.
papers.abstract: Nuclear receptor ligand interaction landscapes remain incompletely characterized, particularly at the scale of entire receptor families. We used Boltz-2, a structure-based deep learning framework for protein-ligand affinity prediction, to perform an unbiased survey of endogenous hormones across all human nuclear receptors. This analysis revealed an asymmetric pattern within steroid hormone receptors: estradiol showed broad predicted compatibility across multiple receptors, whereas other steroid hormones did not exhibit reciprocal compatibility with estrogen receptors. To interpret this pattern
papers.summary: This study uses Boltz-2, a deep learning tool for protein-ligand affinity prediction, to map interactions between endogenous hormones and all human nuclear receptors. It finds that estradiol is predicted to bind broadly across multiple receptors, while other steroid hormones do not show reciprocal compatibility with estrogen receptors, suggesting an evolutionary buffer between estrogen and androgen signaling.

papers.title: Kinetics, thermodynamics, and mechanisms of PMO interactions from computational molecular modeling.
papers.abstract: Phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligonucleotides (PMOs) are a class of antisense oligonucleotides. While PMOs have enabled several nucleic acid therapeutics, their structural and energetic solution properties remain poorly understood. Using solution viscosity measurements combined with computational molecular modeling, we explored interactions of therapeutic 22-mer, 25-mer, and 30-mer PMOs in concentrated solutions. Self-association of PMO monomers involves non-specific interactions, is energetically favorable (with estimates of -32 to -67 kcal/mol interaction energies), and exhibits biphasic ki
papers.summary: This study uses computational molecular modeling and viscosity measurements to characterize how phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligonucleotides (PMOs) interact in solution, revealing that PMO self-association is energetically favorable and involves non-specific interactions. The findings provide new structural and energetic insights into PMO behavior, which could inform the design of more effective antisense therapeutics.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics characterisation of RSPO2+ nucleus pulposus cells reveals a WNT/FN1-CD44 degenerative axis and therapeutic targets in IVDD.
papers.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a common cause of chronic low back pain, imposing a significant economic and physiological burden on individuals and society worldwide. Although dysregulation of the WNT/β-catenin pathway is considered an important factor contributing to the dysfunction of nucleus pulposus (NP) cells and degradation of the extracellular matrix, the mechanisms by which specific subgroups of NP cells are activated and the maintenance of excessive activation of specific pathways remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize RSPO2+ nucleus pulposus cells in intervertebral disc degeneration, identifying a WNT/FN1-CD44 degenerative axis that drives disease progression. The findings reveal potential therapeutic targets within this axis for treating IVDD.

papers.title: Phytochemical Profiling and Antibacterial Activity of Moroccan Monofloral Honeys Against Multidrug-Resistant Uropathogens: In Vitro, ADMET, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Approaches.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections represent a significant public health issue exacerbated by bacterial antibiotic resistance. Honey, due to its phenolic compounds, offers a promising natural alternative. This study explores the phenolic profile of monofloral honeys from the Beni Mellal-Khenifra region and their antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant strains. Four monofloral honeys from Beni Mellal-Khenifra were analyzed for their phenolic composition and evaluated for antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant uropathogenic bacteria. Computational studies were also performed to expl
papers.summary: This study profiles the phenolic compounds in four Moroccan monofloral honeys and tests their antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant uropathogenic bacteria, finding promising effects. Computational docking and dynamics simulations further suggest that specific phenolic compounds may act as antibacterial agents, supporting honey's potential as a natural alternative for treating resistant urinary tract infections.

papers.title: Virtual single-cell perturbation and genetic causal inference reveal CSF1R-dependent immunometabolic communication in iron metabolism-associated osteoarthritis.
papers.abstract: Iron dysregulation has emerged as a contributor to osteoarthritis (OA), yet the cell-communication mechanisms connecting iron-related genetic signals to joint degeneration remain insufficiently defined. Here, we established an integrative computational framework combining transcriptomic screening, machine learning, Mendelian randomization, immune and metabolite mediation analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, virtual gene perturbation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental validation to identify signaling regulators involved in iron metabolism-associated OA. By int
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative computational framework combining transcriptomics, machine learning, Mendelian randomization, single-cell analysis, and virtual perturbation to identify CSF1R as a key regulator of iron metabolism-associated osteoarthritis. The findings reveal CSF1R-dependent immunometabolic communication between immune cells and chondrocytes, providing a potential therapeutic target for OA.

papers.title: Glucose Oxidoreductases for Glucose Monitoring: A Bird's Eye View of Glucose-Sensing Enzymes II.
papers.abstract: Biosensors, utilizing glucose oxidoreductases as biological recognition elements (BREs), underpin current blood glucose monitoring (BGM) and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) technologies. Glucose oxidase remains the gold standard due to its high selectivity and stability, yet its oxygen dependency limits it to first- and second-generation sensing. Fungal flavin adenine dinucletotide (FAD)-dependent glucose dehydrogenase (GDH) has emerged as the standard for mediator-based second-generation sensors due to its oxygen insensitivity, though it requires further engineering to match the stability
papers.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
papers.summary: This review provides an overview of glucose oxidoreductases used in blood glucose monitoring and continuous glucose monitoring systems, highlighting glucose oxidase as the gold standard due to its selectivity and stability, while noting its oxygen dependency. It also discusses fungal FAD-dependent glucose dehydrogenase as a promising alternative for mediator-based sensors due to its oxygen insensitivity, though further engineering is needed to improve stability.

papers.title: Toward Rational Design of Precision-Fermented Milk Proteins: Integrating Cross-Species Selection, Post-Translational Modification, and AI Optimization.
papers.abstract: Milk proteins deliver nutritional, functional, and bioactive properties that alternative protein sources cannot adequately replicate, yet conventional livestock-based production faces compounding constraints of scalability, resource intensity, and sustainability. Precision fermentation offers a structurally distinct solution, but existing reviews have addressed neither a systematic cross-species framework for target selection nor a treatment of post-translational modifications (PTMs) gap-bridging, leaving critical gaps in rational pipeline design. This review integrates four analyses: a cross-
papers.journal: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety
papers.summary: This review proposes a rational design framework for precision-fermented milk proteins, integrating cross-species selection, post-translational modification considerations, and AI-driven optimization to address scalability and sustainability challenges. It fills a gap by providing a systematic approach to target selection and PTM bridging in precision fermentation pipelines.

papers.title: Development of new imidazopyridine-based chalcones hybrids as potent antidiabetic and antioxidant agents: synthesis, in silico and in vitro evaluation.
papers.abstract: Nowadays, diabetes mellitus (DM) is a rapidly growing global health concern. In this study, we synthesized a novel series of six imidazopyridine-based chalcone hybrids (5a-f) and evaluated their in vitro biological activities, including total antioxidant capacity, iron-reducing power, and radical scavenging (DPPH, ABTS, NO), as well as antidiabetic potential against α-amylase, α-glucosidase, and aldose reductase. All compounds showed moderate to potent activity, with derivatives 5c and 5f being the most effective. Compound 5f exhibited the highest antioxidant performance (total capacity: 78.63
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis of six new imidazopyridine-based chalcone hybrids and evaluates their antioxidant and antidiabetic activities in vitro. Several compounds, especially 5c and 5f, showed potent activity against key diabetes-related enzymes and strong antioxidant effects, suggesting they are promising leads for further drug development.

papers.title: A computational framework integrating a protein language model with alchemical simulation for gain-of-function enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Engineering enzymes with enhanced activity and stability is a central goal of biotechnology, yet the inherent trade-off between optimizing global protein fitness and specific substrate binding affinity poses a significant challenge. Here, we present ESM-FEP, a computational framework that synergistically integrates a fine-tuned protein language model with alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) to overcome this limitation. Our workflow employs a parameter-efficient fine-tuned ESM-2 model to perform high-throughput saturation mutagenesis, rapidly identifying mutations that preserve protein fi
papers.summary: This paper introduces ESM-FEP, a computational framework that combines a fine-tuned protein language model (ESM-2) with alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) to design enzymes with enhanced activity and stability. The approach addresses the trade-off between global protein fitness and substrate binding affinity by using the language model for high-throughput saturation mutagenesis screening and FEP for precise binding affinity evaluation. This integrated strategy offers a promising solution for gain-of-function enzyme engineering.

papers.title: Methionine γ-lyase traps cofactor pyridoxal-5'-phosphate through specific serine-mediated affinity.
papers.abstract: Pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP), the ubiquitous and ancient cofactor, plays important roles in enzymatic elimination, transamination and other reactions. The catalytic efficiency of PLP-dependent enzymes is significantly higher than that of free PLP. The recruitment of solution PLP by the enzymes, particularly through interactions outside the active-site entrance, is the key step determining the occurrence of PLP-mediated catalysis. However, the precise mechanism by which enzymes recruit solution PLP remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study reveals a specific serine-mediated mechanism by which methionine γ-lyase traps its cofactor pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP), providing new insights into how PLP-dependent enzymes recruit this essential cofactor from solution. The findings highlight the importance of interactions outside the active-site entrance in determining catalytic efficiency.

papers.title: Deep mutational scanning of CYP2C9, CYP2C19, and NUDT15 shows that pharmacogene variant interpretation requires assay-specific functional data.
papers.abstract: Pharmacogene missense variants can disrupt protein stability, catalytic competence, or substrate handling through distinct mechanisms. General-purpose predictors estimate clinical pathogenicity as a single scalar, whereas pharmacogene interpretation requires knowing which biochemical dimension a variant perturbs, since that determines whether reduced function is substrate-dependent. Five deep mutational scanning datasets comprising 26,198 missense variants across CYP2C9, CYP2C19, and NUDT15 were assembled from MaveDB. Paired assays showed that this dimensionality dominates the data: 28% of CYP
papers.summary: This study compiles deep mutational scanning data for pharmacogenes CYP2C9, CYP2C19, and NUDT15, revealing that variant effects are assay-specific and often substrate-dependent. The findings emphasize that pharmacogene interpretation requires functional data from multiple assays rather than relying on general-purpose pathogenicity predictors.

papers.title: Evaluating molecular docking for binding affinity predictions: a systematic analysis of key parameters and the utility of AlphaFold2 structures for the Schrödinger dataset.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is one of the most established methods in computational drug discovery, due to its balance of speed and accuracy. However, the accuracy of docking results depends on a number of different parameters, and systematic reference data for comparisons to more advanced methods for binding affinity prediction are still scarce. This study assesses the impact of key parameters on the accuracy of binding free energy estimates from docking, using nine benchmark systems with 278 high-affinity ligands. Using the Molecular Operating Environment (MOE), we evaluated combinations of three rece
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates how key docking parameters affect binding affinity predictions using nine benchmark systems with 278 high-affinity ligands, and tests whether AlphaFold2-generated protein structures can substitute for experimental structures in docking workflows. The findings provide practical guidance for optimizing docking settings and highlight the utility and limitations of AlphaFold2 structures for virtual screening.

papers.title: Conserved protein folds underpin the diversification of secreted proteins in a fungal pathogen.
papers.abstract: During host colonization, fungal plant pathogens secrete effector-like proteins that alter host cell physiology and target plant-associated microbes. However, rapid evolution and low sequence conservation hinder the study and characterization of these proteins. The fungus Zymoseptoria passerinii infects Hordeum spp. and includes lineages adapted to wild and domesticated barley. To date, the evolution of effector-like proteins in this species has not been addressed.
papers.summary: This study investigates the evolution of secreted effector-like proteins in the fungal pathogen Zymoseptoria passerinii, which infects barley species. Despite rapid sequence divergence, the authors find that conserved protein folds underpin the diversification of these proteins, providing a framework for characterizing effectors that lack sequence similarity.

papers.title: Exploring the mechanism of Shengmai San in treating lung adenocarcinoma based on bioinformatics and molecular dynamics simulation.
papers.abstract: To investigate the mechanism of Shengmai San (SMS) in the treatment of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) based on an integrated strategy combining "network pharmacology, bioinformatics, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation," aiming to provide a precise combination therapy strategy and identify potential bioactive compounds. Differentially expressed genes in LUAD were identified from the Gene Expression Omnibus database using R (originally developed at Bell Laboratories and currently managed by Lucent Technologies). SMS components (ginseng, Ophiopogon japonicus, and Schisandra chinensi
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, bioinformatics, and molecular dynamics simulations to explore how the traditional Chinese medicine formula Shengmai San may act against lung adenocarcinoma. It identifies differentially expressed genes and potential bioactive compounds, suggesting a multi-target mechanism that could inform combination therapy strategies.

papers.title: Discovery of two novel small-molecule series with potent SARS-CoV-2 inhibition via putative nsp13 open-state trapping.
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of 31 SARS-CoV-2 inhibitors identified across two computational-to-experimental screening campaigns, with average cell-based antiviral potency satisfying 〈EC50〉 ≤ CC50/3 in A549-hACE2 cells. These compounds were selected from 60 successfully tested molecules evaluated using nanoluciferase reporter assay (nLuc), cytopathic effect (CPE), and host-cell cytotoxicity (CC50) assays. We used a funnel-like computational framework where candidate compounds were progressively prioritized through different scores, improving robustness against the limitations of individual metrics.
papers.summary: This paper reports the discovery of 31 SARS-CoV-2 inhibitors from two computational-to-experimental screening campaigns, with promising antiviral potency in cell-based assays. The compounds were identified using a funnel-like computational framework that progressively prioritized candidates, and the study highlights two novel small-molecule series that may act by trapping the viral nsp13 helicase in an open state.

papers.title: Hexachlorobutadiene exposure promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression via CD8+ T dysfunction and VDR-mediated PI3K/AKT activation: An integrated multi-omics and experimental study.
papers.abstract: Hexachlorobutadiene (HCBD), a persistent organic pollutant listed under the Stockholm Convention, has raised increasing concern due to its potential health risks; however, its role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression remains unclear. In this study, we systematically investigated the toxicological effects and underlying mechanisms of HCBD in HCC progression using an integrated computational and experimental framework. Network toxicology analysis identified 139 shared targets between HCBD exposure and HCC, which were enriched in pathways related to xenobiotic metabolism, oncogenic sign
papers.summary: This study shows that the environmental pollutant hexachlorobutadiene (HCBD) promotes liver cancer progression by suppressing CD8+ T cell function and activating the PI3K/AKT pathway through the vitamin D receptor (VDR). Using a combination of network toxicology, multi-omics, and experimental validation, the authors provide evidence that HCBD exposure may be a risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma.

papers.title: Minimal organism JCVI-syn3.0, an engineered derivative of Mycoplasma mycoides, encodes an assortment of unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors.
papers.abstract: In 2016, researchers at the J. Craig Venter Institute produced JCVI-Syn3.0, a derivative of Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri Large Colony strain GM12 with a re-engineered, minimized genome. The minimal synthetic genome of 532 kbp encodes 473 genes, selected from ∼910 parent genes on the basis of their indispensability, that is, a lethal phenotype caused by a knockout of each such gene. Among these genes, 438 genes encode proteins, of which ∼150 were not assigned a molecular function or predicted cellular role. A decade later, despite community annotation efforts, 50-60 of these putative protei
papers.summary: This study re-analyzes the minimal genome of JCVI-syn3.0 and identifies previously uncharacterized membrane transporters and immunity factors encoded by its 473 genes. The findings suggest that even the simplest synthetic organism harbors unrecognized functional proteins, highlighting gaps in current functional annotation and potential for discovery.

papers.title: Rational design of naphtho[2,3-d]imidazole-4,9-dione-linked 1,3,4-oxadiazoles as α-amylase inhibitors supported by QSAR, docking, molecular dynamics, and ADME approaches.
papers.abstract: A new series of 1,3,4-oxadiazole derivatives linked to naphtho[2,3-d]imidazole-4,9-dione were designed, synthesized, and evaluated for their α-amylase inhibitory activity through both in vitro and in silico methods. The compounds were synthesized via cyclization of (E/Z)-N'-(aryl/heteroarylbenzylidene)-2-(4,9-dioxo-4,9-dihydro-1H-naphtho[2,3-d]imidazole-1-yl)acetohydrazides (8a-8aa) with iodobenzene diacetate (IBD) in dichloromethane (DCM). The structures of the synthesized compounds were confirmed using various spectroscopic techniques. The in vitro testing revealed that several derivatives,
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of novel naphtho[2,3-d]imidazole-4,9-dione-linked 1,3,4-oxadiazoles as potential α-amylase inhibitors, combining in vitro assays with computational methods (QSAR, docking, molecular dynamics, ADME). Several derivatives showed promising inhibitory activity, supported by in silico predictions of binding and drug-like properties.

papers.title: Polyunsaturated fatty acid synthase: structure, mechanism and applications for sustainable polyunsaturated fatty acid production.
papers.abstract: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) play critical roles in human growth and development, visual and neurological function, and cardiovascular health, and are widely used in the food, pharmaceutical, and other industries. Traditional PUFA sources are primarily derived from deep-sea fish, which are constrained by fishery resources and environmental pollution, highlighting the urgent need for sustainable production methods. The anaerobic polyketide synthase pathway mediated by PUFA synthase in marine microorganisms efficiently synthesizes docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), a
papers.summary: This review covers the structure, mechanism, and biotechnological applications of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) synthases, which enable sustainable production of DHA and EPA without relying on fish oil. It highlights the potential of these enzymes for industrial-scale, environmentally friendly PUFA manufacturing.

papers.title: Design and evaluation of novel fluorescein hydrazone derivatives as efficient corrosion inhibitors for carbon steel in acidic media: experimental and computational studies.
papers.abstract: A novel O-allylated fluorescein hydrazone derivative was synthesized from fluorescein through a three-step synthetic route. The synthesis route involved an initial hydrazinolysis of fluorescein to obtain fluorescein hydrazide (FH), followed by condensation with p-chlorobenzaldehyde to produce fluorescein hydrazone (FHB). The obtained hydrazone was subsequently O-alkylated with allyl bromide to afford O-allylated fluorescein hydrazone (FHBA). All the synthesized products were thoroughly characterized by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). The corrosion inhi
papers.summary: This paper describes the synthesis and characterization of novel fluorescein hydrazone derivatives and evaluates their effectiveness as corrosion inhibitors for carbon steel in acidic environments. Using experimental and computational methods, the study demonstrates that these compounds provide significant corrosion protection, with the O-allylated derivative showing the highest efficiency.

papers.title: Molecular recognition of a Novel thiazolidinedione-morpholine-based ionic liquid salt by HSA: spectroscopic and molecular dynamics analysis.
papers.abstract: Human serum albumin (HSA) is the most abundant transport protein in human plasma and plays a crucial role in the pharmacokinetic behavior of therapeutic agents. In the present study, the interaction between a newly synthesized thiazolidinedione-morpholine-based ionic liquid salt (TMH-IL) and HSA was systematically investigated using spectroscopic techniques in combination with molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Steady-state fluorescence spectroscopy revealed concentration-dependent quenching of the intrinsic fluorescence of HSA. Temperature-dependent Stern-Volmer analys
papers.summary: This study characterizes how a newly synthesized thiazolidinedione-morpholine-based ionic liquid salt binds to human serum albumin (HSA), the main transport protein in blood. Using fluorescence spectroscopy, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors show that the compound quenches HSA's intrinsic fluorescence in a concentration-dependent manner, indicating a specific interaction. The work provides insights into the binding behavior of this potential therapeutic agent, which could inform its pharmacokinetic profile.

papers.title: De-Nterm-ining GLP1R signaling bias.
papers.abstract: Biased agonism has emerged as a promising strategy for improving incretin therapeutics, yet the structural determinants of signaling bias remain incompletely understood. Building on their recent parathyroid hormone 1 receptor-β-arrestin structure, Zhao and colleagues identify extracellular loop 3 as a conformational switch controlling glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor transducer selectivity, enabling rational design of biased agonists.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses a recent study identifying extracellular loop 3 as a key structural switch that controls signaling bias in the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R). The finding enables rational design of biased agonists, potentially improving incretin-based therapies for metabolic diseases.

papers.title: Structure-Guided Optimization of a Molecular Glue Targeting the KBTBD4-HDAC1/2 Complex.
papers.abstract: Optimization of UM171, a molecular glue initiating the degradation of neosubstrate HDAC1/2-CoREST-LSD1 through a multiprotein complex formed with KBTBD4, was carried out using the cryo-EM structure of its KBTBD4-HDAC2 complex. Structural modifications resulted in a 20-fold improvement in glue activity, demonstrated by the stability of its ternary complex with KBTBD4-HDAC2. These improvements were also accompanied by a robust degradation of LSD1 and the CoREST1 protein. Our results, although promising, also highlight the complexity of structure-guided glue design. The effect of the developed gl
papers.summary: This study used the cryo-EM structure of the KBTBD4-HDAC2 complex to guide optimization of UM171, a molecular glue that degrades HDAC1/2-CoREST-LSD1. Structural modifications led to a 20-fold improvement in glue activity, with enhanced ternary complex stability and robust degradation of LSD1 and CoREST1. The findings underscore both the promise and complexity of structure-guided molecular glue design.

papers.title: Prenatal urinary phenanthrene metabolites associated with fetal growth restriction: a nested case-control study with integrated computational toxicology.
papers.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are ubiquitous environmental pollutants that can cross the placental barrier, yet evidence linking internal exposure to specific PAH metabolites with fetal growth restriction (FGR) remains scarce and mechanistically unclear. In a nested case-control study within a prospective birth cohort in Guangzhou, China (100 FGR cases and 194 matched controls), we quantified maternal urinary hydroxylated and aminated PAH metabolites in first-trimester samples by HPLC-MS/MS. Conditional logistic regression with machine learning was used to identify PAH metabolites as
papers.summary: This study found that higher maternal urinary levels of certain phenanthrene metabolites in the first trimester were associated with increased risk of fetal growth restriction (FGR) in a Chinese cohort. Using machine learning and computational toxicology, the authors identified specific PAH metabolites as potential contributors and explored possible mechanisms, providing new evidence linking environmental PAH exposure to adverse birth outcomes.

papers.title: Evaluating the outputs of ARAE-based molecular generative model for synthetic accessibility and BTK inhibition.
papers.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies in drug discovery represents a rapidly expanding area of interest, providing a valuable means for exploring uncharted chemical spaces to identify novel therapeutic candidates. In this proof-of-concept study, we evaluated hypothetical drug-like molecules generated by an adversarial regularized autoencoder (ARAE) architecture, which were not documented in existing chemical literature and databases, for their synthetic tractability and inhibitory effects on Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). Utilizing a structure-based computational appro
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study evaluates novel drug-like molecules generated by an adversarial regularized autoencoder (ARAE) for their synthetic accessibility and potential to inhibit Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). Using structure-based computational methods, the authors assess whether AI-generated compounds that are absent from existing chemical databases can be viable therapeutic candidates.

papers.title: Lanthanum-Doped Hollow Metallo-Borospherene: La3B23.
papers.abstract: Lanthanide-doped boron clusters constitute a novel paradigm in chemistry, disrupting conventional structural models through unprecedented electron delocalization and geometric reconfiguration. Herein, we conducted an extensive computational investigation on the La3B23 - cluster, revealing a cage-like metallo-borospherene global minimum with D 3h symmetry, where the B23 scaffold consists of two B10 triangular units connected via three bridging boron atoms, forming three shared B10 rings each occupied by one La atom. Chemical bonding analysis reveals that the high symmetry and stability of the c
papers.summary: This computational study identifies a new lanthanum-doped boron cluster, La3B23-, which adopts a cage-like metallo-borospherene structure with high symmetry (D3h). The cluster's stability arises from unique electron delocalization and geometric arrangement, offering insights into novel boron-based nanomaterials.

papers.title: Mining of Novel Human DPP-IV-Targeting Tripeptides through Multicomputational Screening and In Vitro Validation for Diabetes Therapy.
papers.abstract: Inhibition of human dipeptidyl peptidase IV (hDPP-IV) is considered an effective strategy in the management of type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the lack of high-throughput screening approaches and the high cost of experimental evaluation have limited the discovery of peptide-based hDPP-IV inhibitors. Herein, an integrated multicomputational screening strategy was employed to successfully mine novel hDPP-IV inhibitory tripeptides. Among the screened candidates, FAW exhibited the highest inhibitory activity, with an IC50 of 233 μM, establishing it as a promising scaffold for further development.
papers.summary: This study used a multi-computational screening approach to identify novel tripeptide inhibitors of human dipeptidyl peptidase IV (hDPP-IV), a key target for type 2 diabetes therapy. The lead candidate, FAW, showed the highest inhibitory activity with an IC50 of 233 μM, providing a promising scaffold for further drug development.

papers.title: Prioritizing Candidate YB‑1 Cold Shock Domain Ligands via 5D-ElectroShape and Boltz Generative Cofolding.
papers.abstract: Y-box binding protein 1 (YB-1) acts as a key oncoprotein, with its highly conserved cold shock domain (CSD) driving core nucleic acid-binding functions in cancer progression. Despite its therapeutic relevance, the CSD is considered "undruggable" due to the lack of a well-defined hydrophobic pocket. To overcome the limitations of rigid docking in this transient pocket, here, we present a computational ligand-prioritization workflow designed to generate experimentally testable hypotheses for this challenging target. We applied the 5D-ElectroShape formalism combined with our in-house MolPrism clu
papers.summary: This study presents a computational workflow to prioritize candidate ligands targeting the cold shock domain (CSD) of the oncoprotein YB-1, which is considered 'undruggable' due to its lack of a stable hydrophobic pocket. The approach combines 5D-ElectroShape shape-based screening with Boltz generative cofolding to overcome limitations of rigid docking in this transient pocket, generating experimentally testable hypotheses. The workflow offers a promising strategy for drug discovery against challenging protein targets with dynamic binding sites.

papers.title: Symphony-Bind: Prediction of Protein Binding Sites for 11 Representative Small Molecules and Ions via Fine-Tuning Protein Language Models and Grouped Multi-Task Learning.
papers.abstract: Accurately identifying protein binding sites for small molecules and ions is crucial for understanding biological processes and advancing drug discovery. Pretrained protein language models (pLMs) have emerged as powerful tools for this purpose, but existing prediction models often face a trade-off when using pLMs: freezing pLMs limits their adaptability, while fully fine-tuning them requires high computational costs. To address this trade-off, we attempted to introduce Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) as a promising solution to balance efficiency and performance. Specifically, we applied
papers.summary: Symphony-Bind is a new computational method that predicts protein binding sites for 11 small molecules and ions by fine-tuning protein language models with parameter-efficient techniques and grouped multi-task learning. It balances prediction accuracy with computational efficiency, offering a practical tool for drug discovery and biological research.

papers.title: [Experimental and computational analyses of altered cetuximab binding induced by EGFR mutations].
papers.abstract: Acquired mutations in the extracellular domain of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) are major causes of cetuximab resistance. However, the structural mechanisms by which different mutations impair antibody binding remain to be clarified. In this study, four clinically reported EGFR mutations, S492R, G465R, S464L, and I491M, were selected for investigation. Corresponding mutant EGFR fusion proteins were constructed, expressed, and purified. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay was performed to evaluate their binding ability to cetuximab. In parallel, SAAMBE-3D, FoldX, and Rosetta were employ
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study investigates how four clinically reported EGFR extracellular domain mutations (S492R, G465R, S464L, I491M) impair cetuximab binding, combining experimental ELISA measurements with computational predictions from SAAMBE-3D, FoldX, and Rosetta. The findings clarify structural mechanisms of acquired resistance to cetuximab, potentially guiding therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: [Screening and characterization of two nanobodies with different CDR3 sequences against porcine CD205].
papers.abstract: The Complementarity-determining region (CDR) is the core region that determines the functions and characteristics of nanobodies. To analyze the impact of the CDR3 region on the developability of nanobodies and antigen-binding activity, this study used two porcine CD205-specific nanobodies (Nb205-1 and Nb205-10) with different CDR3 regions as models and compared them in terms of prokaryotic expression, Ni column purification, and antigen binding, providing references for the screening and evaluation of nanobodies. Phage display technology was employed to screen porcine CD205-specific nanobodies
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study screened and characterized two nanobodies targeting porcine CD205 that differ in their CDR3 sequences, comparing their expression, purification, and antigen-binding properties. The findings provide insight into how CDR3 variability affects nanobody developability and binding activity, offering guidance for nanobody screening and evaluation.

papers.title: Advances in Carrageenases: Molecular Engineering, Immobilization Techniques, and Biomedical Potential of Carrageenan Oligosaccharides.
papers.abstract: Carrageenan is a sulfated polysaccharide extracted from red algae, widely utilized in the food and pharmaceutical industries due to its unique gelling properties and biological activities. However, its high molecular weight and low solubility limit certain high-value applications. Carrageenases specifically degrade carrageenan to produce low-molecular-weight oligosaccharides with excellent bioactivities, thereby overcoming this bottleneck. This review systematically summarizes the microbial sources of carrageenases and the classification characteristics of their three types (κ, ι, and λ) withi
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in carrageenases, including their microbial sources, classification into κ, ι, and λ types, molecular engineering, and immobilization strategies. It also highlights the biomedical potential of carrageenan oligosaccharides, which are produced by enzymatic degradation and exhibit improved bioactivities. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of how these enzymes can overcome the limitations of native carrageenan for high-value applications.

papers.title: Targeting the PHB2-ACSL3 Lipid-Remodeling Axis Overcomes Cisplatin Resistance by Restoring Ferroptosis in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapy resistance remains a major obstacle in gastric cancer (GC) treatment. Through integrated transcriptomic profiling of cisplatin-resistant xenografts and pharmacogenomic interrogation of the NCI-60 dataset, we identified Prohibitin-2 (PHB2) as a previously unrecognized determinant of chemoresistance. PHB2 was consistently upregulated in resistant tumors and associated with poor clinical outcomes. Mechanistically, PHB2 binds the lipid-metabolic enzyme ACSL3 through a defined AMP-binding-domain interface (residues W244/H254/E260), enhancing ACSL3 activity to promote mon
papers.summary: This study identifies PHB2 as a driver of cisplatin resistance in gastric cancer by binding to and enhancing ACSL3 activity, which promotes lipid remodeling that suppresses ferroptosis. Targeting the PHB2-ACSL3 axis restores ferroptosis and overcomes chemoresistance, offering a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: N/P-Dependent DNA Complexation, Transfection, and Cytotoxicity of Imine-Linked Low-Molecular-Weight PEI Polyplexes.
papers.abstract: Gene delivery with cationic polymers requires balancing DNA compaction, colloidal stability, and intracellular release, yet for imine-linked low-molecular-weight polyethyleneimine (PEI) vectors, quantitative relationships connecting the N/P ratio with the full property-transfection cascade remain undefined. Here, two amphiphilic non-viral vectors were prepared by linking a hydrophobic benzene-siloxane core (TAS) to hyperbranched PEI (800 or 2000 Da) through reversible imine bonds and complexed with DNA across a broad N/P range (10-600). Polyplexes were characterized by atomic force microscopy
papers.summary: This study examines how the N/P ratio affects DNA binding, transfection efficiency, and cytotoxicity for imine-linked low-molecular-weight PEI vectors. The authors prepared two amphiphilic polymers and characterized their polyplexes across a wide N/P range, revealing quantitative relationships that could guide the design of safer and more effective gene delivery vehicles.

papers.title: Physicochemical and Metabolic Optimization of NAMPT Inhibitors Enables Effective Antibody-Drug Conjugates for Liquid and Solid Tumors.
papers.abstract: Antibody drug conjugates (ADCs) enable selective delivery of highly potent small molecules, yet most clinically validated payloads target solely cell-division pathways with several drawbacks such as high off-target toxicity and a lack of efficacy on nondividing tumor cells (e.g., tumor stem cells). Metabolic targets such as nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT) offer a complementary mode of action and are predestined as ADC payloads since systemic toxicities have prevented clinical use of NAMPT inhibitors (NAMPTi) as free drugs. Here we show that highly hydrophobic NAMPTi, especially
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that optimizing the physicochemical and metabolic properties of NAMPT inhibitors enables their effective use as antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) payloads, showing efficacy against both liquid and solid tumors. The approach offers a complementary mechanism to traditional cell-division-targeting payloads, potentially addressing limitations like off-target toxicity and efficacy against non-dividing tumor cells.

papers.title: Rational Engineering of AKR13B3 from Devosia A6-243 for Enhanced Aflatoxin B1 Degradation: A Dual Mechanism of Substrate Polarization and Tunnel Remodeling.
papers.abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is one of the most toxic mycotoxins, widely contaminating agricultural products and posing a serious threat to food safety and human health. Enzymatic degradation is considered a promising detoxification strategy due to its high efficiency, strong specificity, and lack of secondary pollution. AKR13B3, a member of the aldo-keto reductase family, possesses intrinsic catalytic activity for AFB1 degradation; however, its low natural activity severely limits practical application. In this study, the binding mode of the AKR13B3-NADPH complex with AFB1 was first determined using A
papers.summary: This study rationally engineered the aldo-keto reductase AKR13B3 from Devosia A6-243 to enhance its ability to degrade the mycotoxin aflatoxin B1 (AFB1). By analyzing the enzyme's structure, the authors identified two key mechanisms—substrate polarization and tunnel remodeling—that improve catalytic activity, offering a promising enzymatic strategy for detoxifying contaminated agricultural products.

papers.title: Precision Covalent Drug Discovery Inspired by Endogenous Electrophilic Signalling in Immune Cells.
papers.abstract: Immune cells possess an intrinsic covalent signalling system in which endogenous electrophilic species function as molecular regulators of cellular state that integrate metabolic activity, oxidative stress, and inflammatory signals. Lipid peroxidation-derived electrophiles, enzymatically generated electrophilic lipid mediators, nitro-fatty acids, and metabolite-derived electrophiles selectively modify reactive amino acid residues within signalling proteins to regulate immune cell differentiation, metabolic adaptation, stress responses, and tissue responses. This perspective highlights that end
papers.summary: This perspective article proposes that the endogenous electrophilic signaling system in immune cells—where reactive lipid and metabolite-derived species covalently modify proteins—can serve as a blueprint for designing precision covalent drugs. By mimicking these natural regulatory mechanisms, new therapeutics could achieve targeted modulation of immune cell function with improved selectivity.

papers.title: Advances in Key Genetic Elements and Strategies for High-Yield Heterologous Protein Expression in Komagataella phaffii.
papers.abstract: Komagataella phaffii has emerged as an important eukaryotic microbial cell factory for the production of industrial enzymes, biopharmaceuticals, and food-related proteins owing to its rapid growth, capacity for eukaryotic post-translational modifications, and suitability for high-cell-density fermentation. However, efficient heterologous protein production remains constrained by limitations in transcriptional regulation, protein secretion, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein-folding capacity. This review summarizes recent advances in engineering key expression elements underlying heterologo
papers.summary: This review discusses recent advances in engineering Komagataella phaffii (a yeast commonly used for producing industrial enzymes and biopharmaceuticals) to improve heterologous protein yields. It focuses on optimizing key genetic elements and strategies to overcome bottlenecks in transcription, secretion, and protein folding in the endoplasmic reticulum.

papers.title: Nicotinamide-Based Covalent Inhibitors of tRNA (m1G37) Methyltransferase (TrmD) to Increase Antibacterial Activity.
papers.abstract: Bacterial tRNA (m1G37) methyltransferase (TrmD) is an essential enzyme required for accurate translation and represents an attractive antibacterial target distinct from its eukaryotic counterpart, Trm5. Here, we describe the development of nicotinamide-based TrmD inhibitors incorporating electrophilic Michael-acceptor motifs to enhance cellular antibacterial activity. Mass spectrometry-based peptide mapping shows covalent modification of TrmD at Cys112, a residue proximal to the AdoMet (S-adenosylmethionine) binding region, providing a mechanistic basis for covalent target engagement. Consiste
papers.summary: This paper describes the development of nicotinamide-based covalent inhibitors targeting the bacterial tRNA methyltransferase TrmD, an essential enzyme for accurate translation and a promising antibacterial target. The inhibitors incorporate Michael-acceptor motifs that covalently modify Cys112 near the AdoMet binding site, enhancing antibacterial activity. Mass spectrometry confirmed the covalent mechanism, offering a new strategy for antibiotic development.

papers.title: Structural and Biophysical Characterization of Aminobenzo[d]isothiazole 1,1-Dioxide SOS1 Ligands.
papers.abstract: SOS1 is a guanine nucleotide exchange factor that promotes KRAS activation by catalyzing GDP release and GTP loading, making SOS1-mediated nucleotide exchange an attractive therapeutic target in KRAS-driven cancers. Herein, we report the synthesis, biophysical characterization, and structural analysis of aminobenzo-[d]-isothiazole 1,1-dioxide SOS1 ligands. Compound 6f engaged SOS1 with a KD of 570 nM by microscale thermophoresis, supported by surface plasmon resonance. X-ray crystal structures of SOS1 bound to compounds 6b and 6f refined previous binding hypotheses regarding pocket engagement.
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis and biophysical characterization of aminobenzo[d]isothiazole 1,1-dioxide compounds as SOS1 ligands, which inhibit KRAS activation. Compound 6f binds SOS1 with a KD of 570 nM, and X-ray structures confirm the binding mode, providing a basis for developing new anticancer therapeutics.

papers.title: Membrane Interfacial Organization Determines the Functional Performance of Liposomal Linezolid.
papers.abstract: Background: Despite extensive development of liposomal antibiotics, the structural determinants governing their stability, release, and biological activity remain poorly understood. This study investigated how the cholesterol content and drug-to-lipid ratio affect membrane organization and thereby determine the physicochemical and biological properties of linezolid-loaded liposomes. Methods: Nine liposomal formulations, varying in their cholesterol content (10-30 wt%) and drug-to-lipid ratios (1-5%), were prepared by thin-film hydration. Membrane organization was analyzed by ATR-FTIR spectrosc
papers.summary: This study examines how cholesterol content and drug-to-lipid ratio affect the membrane organization of liposomal linezolid, and how these structural features influence stability, release, and antibacterial activity. Using ATR-FTIR and other analyses, the authors identify specific membrane interfacial properties that correlate with improved formulation performance, providing a rational basis for designing more effective liposomal antibiotics.

papers.title: Beyond Composition: Structure-Activity Relationships in Bioactive Deep Eutectic Systems.
papers.abstract: Deep eutectic systems (DESs) have evolved from sustainable solvent alternatives to promising bioactive platforms with reported antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, regenerative, cryoprotective, and cytoprotective properties. However, despite the growing number of biological studies, the mechanistic basis of these effects remains poorly understood because biological activity is still interpreted predominantly from the chemical identity of the hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor, rather than from the supramolecular organization of the eutectic system itself. This review is intended to provide anyone i
papers.summary: This review argues that the biological activity of deep eutectic systems (DESs) depends not only on their chemical composition but also on their supramolecular structure, and calls for a shift toward structure-activity relationship studies. It highlights the need to understand the mechanistic basis of DES bioactivities such as antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory effects, which remain poorly characterized.

papers.title: Combining Triazole Scaffold Repurposing and Generative Transformer Architecture for Structure-Based Inhibitor Design Targeting the LasR Quorum Sensing Receptor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.abstract: Background: The rapid escalation of multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa necessitates anti-virulence strategies targeting quorum sensing rather than bacterial survival; however, integrating scaffold repurposing with generative AI to inhibit LasR remains underexplored. Here, we address this gap by combining triazole scaffold mining with transformer-based de novo molecular generation to systematically identify putative LasR inhibitors. Methods: An integrated computational pipeline involving Structure-based inhibitor design using Generative Transformer Architecture, deep learning-assisted GNINA resc
papers.summary: This study presents a computational pipeline that combines triazole scaffold repurposing with a generative transformer architecture to design novel inhibitors of the LasR quorum sensing receptor in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, an anti-virulence strategy against multidrug-resistant infections. The approach integrates structure-based drug design with deep learning-based rescoring to identify promising lead compounds, offering a new avenue for combating antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Recombinant Thermostable DNA Polymerases: Current Approaches to Production, Molecular Engineering, and Applications in Biotechnology and Diagnostics.
papers.abstract: DNA polymerases are crucial for the replication and repair of genetic material. Advances in recombinant DNA technology and protein engineering have enabled the production of enzymes with specific catalytic properties tailored to the requirements of molecular diagnostics, next-generation sequencing, and synthetic biology. This review discusses the classification and structural-functional organization of DNA polymerases, with an emphasis on the thermostable members of Families A and B, which are of great practical importance. The main systems for heterologous expression and methods for purifying
papers.summary: This review covers the production, engineering, and applications of recombinant thermostable DNA polymerases, focusing on Families A and B. It discusses heterologous expression systems, purification methods, and how engineered enzymes are tailored for diagnostics, next-generation sequencing, and synthetic biology.

papers.title: ERβ-Score: An Interpretable Machine Learning-Based Scoring Function and Web Server for Estrogen Receptor β-Guided Drug Discovery in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most clinically aggressive subtype of breast cancer, characterized by the absence of targetable hormone receptors and HER2 amplification, significantly constraining treatment choices. Estrogen Receptor Beta (ERβ) has emerged as a biologically relevant yet underutilized target in TNBC, with its re-expression linked to tumor suppression and improved prognosis, prompting the development of selective ERβ modulators as a precision therapeutic approach. We introduce ERβ-Score, an interpretable machine learning scoring system developed using a curated datas
papers.summary: The authors present ERβ-Score, an interpretable machine learning-based scoring function and web server designed to support drug discovery targeting Estrogen Receptor Beta (ERβ) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The tool aims to identify selective ERβ modulators by leveraging a curated dataset, potentially aiding in the development of precision therapies for this aggressive cancer subtype.

papers.title: Virtual Screening-Guided Identification of Candidate USP7-Inhibitory Scaffolds Exhibiting Antiproliferative Activity.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ubiquitin-specific protease 7 (USP7) is a deubiquitinating enzyme that regulates multiple oncogenic and tumor-suppressive pathways and has emerged as a promising target for anticancer drug discovery. However, most reported USP7 inhibitors belong to a limited number of structural classes, and no USP7-targeted therapy has yet reached clinical application. This study aimed to identify structurally diverse candidate USP7-inhibitory scaffolds with antiproliferative activity using an integrated computational and experimental screening strategy. Methods: A drug discovery workfl
papers.summary: This study used an integrated computational and experimental screening approach to identify structurally diverse small-molecule inhibitors of USP7, a deubiquitinating enzyme implicated in cancer. The authors discovered candidate scaffolds with antiproliferative activity, expanding the chemical space of potential USP7-targeted anticancer agents.

papers.title: Active ingredients of Astragalus-ginseng against COPD-associated sarcopenia: network pharmacology and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)-associated sarcopenia is a critical comorbidity associated with high morbidity and mortality, driven by chronic systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and proteometabolic dysregulation. The Astragalus membranaceus-Ginseng (HQ-RS) herbal pair is a traditional remedy for consumptive diseases; however, its molecular mechanisms against this comorbidity remain undefined.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular dynamics simulations to identify active ingredients in the Astragalus-ginseng herbal pair that may combat COPD-associated sarcopenia. It reveals potential key compounds and protein targets involved in inflammation and muscle metabolism pathways, offering a mechanistic basis for this traditional remedy.

papers.title: Decoding astrocytic tryptophan metabolism in the pathogenesis of epilepsy: evidence from artificial intelligence-driven multi-omics and clinical validation.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy (EP) is a prevalent neurological disorder with complex etiology, often involving metabolic dysregulation. Emerging evidence highlights the role of tryptophan metabolism (TM) and astrocyte dysfunction in EP pathogenesis. This study aimed to decode the TM and astrocyte (TA)-related molecular signature and identify a central therapeutic target for EP.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of tryptophan metabolism and astrocyte dysfunction in epilepsy using AI-driven multi-omics analysis and clinical validation. It identifies a molecular signature and a potential central therapeutic target, suggesting that targeting astrocytic tryptophan metabolism could offer new treatment avenues for epilepsy.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven Bioprospecting of Cholinergic Medicinal Plants for Putative Leads Against Butyrylcholinesterase Towards Alzheimer's Care.
papers.abstract: Butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) plays a key role in preserving appropriate cholinergic neurotransmission that is essentially altered in the brains of advanced Alzheimer's disease (AD), hence a therapeutic target. This study employed a machine learning (ML) bioactivity predictive model to explore the chemical space of potential BChE inhibitors. A cheminformatics pipeline was explored to create a ML model for BChE inhibition using structural insights complemented with a comprehensive variance importance plot (VIP) and correlation matrix analysis. Specifically, a compiled library of 2179 secondary m
papers.summary: This study used machine learning to build a predictive model for butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) inhibition, screening medicinal plants for potential Alzheimer's disease leads. The model identified promising plant-derived compounds, offering a cost-effective approach for drug discovery targeting advanced Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of DENV-1 Isolates From Pakistan Reveals Immunogenic Variability and Antiviral Potential of Phytochemicals Targeting the CprM Region.
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV), a mosquito-borne arbovirus, remains a critical global health concern, causing approximately 390 million infections annually. Dengue fever poses significant challenges to healthcare systems in endemic regions like Pakistan due to the presence of four established serotypes (DENV-1-DENV-4) and the potential emergence of a fifth serotype (DENV-5). The current study aimed to investigate molecular characteristics of DENV-1 isolates from Peshawar, Pakistan, focusing on serotyping, genetic variability in the CprM junction region, and identification of potential antiviral phytochem
papers.summary: This study characterizes DENV-1 isolates from Pakistan by examining genetic variability in the CprM junction region, revealing immunogenic differences among strains. The authors also identify phytochemicals with potential antiviral activity targeting this region, suggesting a possible avenue for drug development against dengue.

papers.title: Computational analysis of CD40L missense variants A123E, S222F, and G257R predicts altered CD40 binding and trimeric stability in X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome.
papers.abstract: CD40L (CD154) is a homotrimeric member of the TNF superfamily protein expressed on activated CD4+ T cells whose interaction with CD40 is required for class-switch recombination, somatic hypermutation, and B cell terminal differentiation. Loss-of-function mutations in gene CD40LG cause X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome type 1 (HIGM1), characterized by recurrent infections, lack of IgG, IgA and IgE, and near-normal or elevated IgM.
papers.summary: This study computationally analyzes three CD40L missense variants (A123E, S222F, G257R) associated with X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome, predicting that they disrupt CD40 binding and trimer stability. These findings provide mechanistic insight into how these mutations impair CD40L function and cause immunodeficiency.

papers.title: Molecular dynamics analysis of a docking-derived baicalein-PPARγ ligand-binding-domain model suggests a pocket-associated AF-2-anchor-silent ensemble.
papers.abstract: Baicalein was examined in a selected docking-derived peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) ligand-binding-domain (LBD) model to test whether pocket association, local helix 12 (H12) organization, and canonical activation function-2 (AF-2) anchoring were coupled under the sampled simulation conditions. Because no baicalein-bound PPARγ cocrystal structure was used, the results are interpreted as a selected-pose molecular dynamics model rather than as a definitive experimental binding mode. Three independent 100-ns replicas were analyzed with bound-state filtering, H12 and AF-2 des
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to explore how baicalein, a natural compound, binds to the PPARγ ligand-binding domain, focusing on whether binding stabilizes the receptor's activation helix. The results suggest that baicalein can occupy the pocket without engaging the canonical AF-2 anchor, implying a non-classical mode of modulation. Since no cocrystal structure was used, the findings are presented as a model-based hypothesis rather than a definitive binding mode.

papers.title: Integrated computational analysis prioritizes candidate targets and pathways linking ochratoxin A exposure to hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Ochratoxin A (OTA), a food-borne mycotoxin, has been implicated in hepatotoxicity and potential carcinogenic processes, yet the molecular links between OTA exposure and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain incompletely understood. This study used an integrated computational workflow to prioritize candidate targets and pathways potentially linking OTA exposure with HCC. OTA-related and HCC-related targets were collected from public databases, intersected, and subjected to functional enrichment analysis. Transcriptomic data from the GSE36376 discovery dataset were analyzed to identify different
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational approach to identify potential molecular targets and pathways linking the food contaminant ochratoxin A (OTA) to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). By intersecting OTA- and HCC-related gene sets and analyzing transcriptomic data, the authors prioritize candidate genes and pathways that may mediate OTA's carcinogenic effects, offering a basis for future experimental validation.

papers.title: Computational identification and evaluation of Adenium obesum phytochemicals as potential EGFR inhibitors for targeted therapy against non-small-cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of lung cancer-related mortality, largely driven by aberrant activation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Despite the clinical success of EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), intrinsic and acquired resistance, coupled with safety concerns, highlight the need for novel, safer inhibitors. Natural products represent an underexplored source of structurally diverse bioactive compounds with favorable biocompatibility. In this study, a comprehensive in silico approach is used to evaluate phytochemicals from Adenium obesum a
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to screen phytochemicals from Adenium obesum as potential inhibitors of EGFR for treating non-small-cell lung cancer. The authors identify promising natural compounds that may serve as safer alternatives to existing EGFR inhibitors, though experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: Multi-Omics and Molecular Simulation Identify KIF11 as a Candidate Direct Target of Resveratrol in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has poor prognosis and variable immunotherapy response. Resveratrol exhibits anti-HCC activity, but its direct targets and association with immunotherapy response are unclear. This study identifies core resveratrol targets in HCC and evaluates their prognostic and predictive value.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics data and molecular simulation to identify KIF11 as a direct target of resveratrol in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), linking it to anti-HCC activity and potential immunotherapy response. The findings suggest KIF11 could serve as a prognostic and predictive biomarker, offering a new avenue for combination therapy in HCC.

papers.title: Body Mass Index and Facial Aging: Mendelian Randomization and Exploratory Target Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Facial aging reflects genetic, metabolic, and environmental influences. Although obesity has been associated with older perceived facial age, the shared genetic basis and direction of the BMI-facial aging relationship remain uncertain.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization to investigate whether body mass index (BMI) causally influences facial aging, finding evidence that higher BMI may affect facial aging traits. It also performs exploratory target prioritization to identify potential genes and pathways linking BMI to facial aging, offering new insights into the genetic and metabolic basis of skin aging.

papers.title: De Novo Molecular Design and Bioactivity Prediction of Novel Hexahydroquinolines as Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (CDPK4) Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (PfCDPK4) is a validated target for malaria transmission-blocking interventions, as its inhibition disrupts male gametocyte exflagellation. Hexahydroquinolines (HHQs) have emerged as promising gametocytocidal agents. This study aimed to design novel HHQs as potential PfCDPK4 inhibitors with good binding affinity, favourable pharmacokinetics, and structural stability. A library of 20,000 novel HHQ analogs was generated using genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design in AlvaBuilder and systematically filtered through a pipeline com
papers.summary: This study used genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design to generate 20,000 novel hexahydroquinoline analogs and filter them for potential inhibitors of Plasmodium falciparum CDPK4, a malaria transmission-blocking target. The pipeline prioritized compounds with good predicted binding affinity, pharmacokinetics, and structural stability, yielding promising candidates for further development.

papers.title: Phycocyanobilin: A potential bioactive compound from Arthrospira platensis targeting LYN protein associated with systemic lupus erythematosus.
papers.abstract: Phycocyanobilin, a bioactive compound derived from Arthrospira platensis C1, was investigated for its potential role in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) based on its structural similarity to bilirubin, with a Tanimoto score of 93%. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinities between phycocyanobilin and several protein targets, including EGFR, FYN, HLA-B, LCK, LYN, and TP53. Target prediction further identified LYN kinase as a key candidate. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable binding of the phycocyanobilin-LYN complex, with interaction profiles comparable to those
papers.summary: This study computationally investigates phycocyanobilin from Arthrospira platensis as a potential therapeutic for systemic lupus erythematosus by targeting the LYN kinase protein. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggest stable binding of phycocyanobilin to LYN, comparable to known interactions, indicating a possible anti-inflammatory mechanism.

papers.title: Pan-cancer profiles of mesothelin (MSLN) unveil diagnostic potential and therapeutic targetability of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Mesothelin (MSLN) is a cell surface glycoprotein that is often over-expressed in various malignancies of humans and has been suggested as a potential therapeutic and diagnostic target. However, its expression profile, clinical implications and drug-targeting potential are not fully understood and needs to be investigated across various cancer types.
papers.summary: This study provides a pan-cancer analysis of mesothelin (MSLN) expression, revealing its overexpression across multiple tumor types and highlighting its diagnostic and therapeutic potential, particularly in pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The findings support MSLN as a promising biomarker and drug target for pancreatic cancer.

papers.title: Discovery of Galangin Derivatives as a Potential T-cell Leukemia Virus 1 Protease Inhibitor Through Chemoinformatics Approaches
papers.summary: This study uses chemoinformatics to identify galangin derivatives as potential inhibitors of the T-cell leukemia virus 1 protease, a key target for treating HTLV-1-associated diseases. The findings suggest these natural compounds could serve as leads for antiviral drug development.
